stem: The timeline shows one session on a QPU. What happens to job 3?

options.text: It waits in the normal queue, then runs in the session and reactivates it.
It fails, because the session was closed when its interactive TTL ran out.
It starts at once: the QPU stays reserved for the session until the max TTL.
It runs as an ordinary job-mode job while the session itself stays deactivated.
It reopens the session, and the maximum TTL timer starts again from zero.

stem.alt: Timeline along a time axis. Job 1 and job 2 run one after another with a short gap between them. After job 2 a bracket marks the interactive TTL; the stretch after it is labelled 'no job'. Later an arrow marks 'job 3 submitted'. A dashed bracket above everything, labelled 'maximum TTL (starts when job 1 starts)', runs from the start of job 1 to a point beyond job 3's submission.

explanation.correct: The two timers do different things. The interactive TTL restarts after every job; when no session job arrives within it, the session is DEACTIVATED — the QPU is released and normal job selection resumes — but it is not closed. The maximum TTL started with job 1 and is still running, so job 3 can reactivate the session; to do so it must go through the normal queue first.

distractors.B: Deactivation is not closing: an inactive session still accepts jobs until its maximum TTL is reached or it is closed explicitly.
distractors.C: The dedicated reservation lasts only while jobs keep arriving within the interactive TTL; after it lapses other users' jobs run, which is why job 3 has to queue.
distractors.D: Job 3 belongs to the session and reactivates it; nothing demotes it to job mode.
distractors.E: The maximum TTL timer starts with the first job and never pauses or resets; reactivation continues the same window.

provenance.notes: R2 add (stem figure, conceptual, d2): interactive TTL lapse deactivates (not closes) a session; job 3 queues normally and reactivates it within the max TTL, which never resets. Source: guides/execution-modes 'Basic workflow' steps 2-3 + note (fetched 2026-10-01). Queueing semantics cannot run locally (local testing mode ignores execution modes).
